items.text: "Switch to non-IT" gets treated online like a single leap.
This is not only about hours.
"I fixed bugs for six years" does not transfer.

blocks.heading: One Blurry "Quit and Figure It Out")

items.text: You teach a subject, a skill, or a professional exam curriculum, in a college, a training company, a coaching institute, or an edtech platform.
People who already get asked "can you explain this simply" at work, and enjoy that more than the technical work itself.

blocks.heading: Run This Before You Pick a Door

items.text: Before you commit money or time to any single door, run your situation through The four questions , your fit, your situation, the job market and AI-proofing, the same fit check that should sit under any real career decision, adapted here for a full exit out of IT.
Teaching a room full of confused students, sitting a competitive exam for a defined number of years, or chasing a first client are each genuinely hard in a different way than IT is hard.
A 26-year-old with no dependents can absorb a year of government-exam prep or a lean freelance start.
Do not resign, enrol in a full-time course, or spend a lakh of rupees before you have tested your fit for real.
Pick one door from the six above based on your honest answers to the four questions.
Start one small, real test on the side: a weekend teaching batch, an SSC or banking mock test under real time pressure, or one small freelance project.

blocks.heading: IT Professionals Are Searching This Right Now
rows: ~68% of Indian IT professionals show 2+ clinical burnout indicators (NASSCOM-Deloitte, 2025)
The exhaustion driving this search is a real, shared industry pattern, not a personal weakness or overreaction.
58% of Indian professionals 35+ have considered a mid-career change in the last 2 years; only ~12% act on it
Wanting out is common. The gap between wanting and doing is usually a missing test plan, not a missing reason.
400,000-500,000 mid-career IT roles projected for restructuring by 2028 (NASSCOM)
Waiting indefinitely for the "right moment" carries its own risk if your current role sits in a legacy-heavy function.
UPSC CSE 2025: ~958 selected out of ~5.8 lakh who appeared (roughly 0.1-0.2% success)
Government-exam doors are real, but treating one exam as your only fallback plan is a genuine financial risk.

blocks.heading: Each Door Really Costs in Year One
rows: Teaching / corporate training
Often a step down initially at a college or coaching institute; corporate trainer and instructional-design roles can be closer to IT pay if you already have delivery experience
Government exams (banking PO, SSC CGL)
Fixed entry pay scale, commonly in the broad Rs 6-11 LPA range once selected, regardless of prior IT salary
Targeting the specific exam and post with the best odds for your profile, not the most prestigious one
HR & L&D
A modest reset or a near-lateral move if the switch happens internally at your current company
A documented mentoring, hiring, or onboarding track record plus a targeted HR certification
Consulting
Wide range; entry-level roles at large firms can pay well but are competitive, while independent consulting income is unpredictable until you build a client base
A specific, provable domain track record and a first paying client before you go independent
Entrepreneurship / freelancing
Near-zero or highly unpredictable income for the first several months, sometimes longer
Starting with one real client or a tested niche before resigning, not launching cold
Non-IT finance roles
A reset toward entry-level finance pay unless you already hold or are close to a relevant certification
A financial-modelling course or CFA-level 1 alongside your current job, before you switch

items.text: Build or confirm an emergency fund covering at least 6-12 months of full household expenses before you resign for a door with an unpredictable early income (entrepreneurship, freelancing, exam prep with no fallback job).
If you are financing a course or exam-prep coaching with savings or a loan, write the actual monthly cost against your realistic post-switch income, not the best-case story from an advertisement.
Separate "I am changing fields" from "I am also taking on new financial risk", doing both fully at once multiplies your risk instead of just adding it.
Fewer dependents usually means you can absorb a lean freelance start, a full government-exam attempt, or a lateral HR move while you build proof.
Age limits for most competitive government exams are still comfortably open in this window, if that door genuinely fits you.
Mistakes here are the cheapest they will ever be, use that window deliberately rather than drifting through it.

blocks.heading: Year and a Lot of Money

items.text: Resigning first and figuring out the door second, with no tested income plan behind the exit.
Chasing "teaching" or "consulting" purely because they sound calmer, without testing whether the actual daily work suits you.
Starting a business or freelance practice with no first client already lined up before quitting.
Collecting certifications for three different doors at once instead of testing one door properly first.
